about: Scored test of event memory (agent/events.py). Run in order with fresh memory: uv run python -m agent.run --sequence [--fake], then uv run python -m agent.evaluate. 'group' says which headlines are the same real-world event; 'expected_event_status' is what the memory should decide. Without memory every exposed headline would alert.

news.headline: Houthi missile attacks force container ships away from the Red Sea
news.body: Major carriers pause transits through the Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb strait after attacks on merchant vessels.
news.why: First report of the Red Sea crisis.

news.headline: Shipping lines extend Red Sea diversions as attacks continue
news.body: Carriers say ships will keep sailing around Africa instead of using the Red Sea route.
news.why: Same situation, same suppliers: no new alert.

news.headline: Fire breaks out at semiconductor plant in Hitachinaka
news.body: A fire at a chip factory in Hitachinaka has halted production.
news.why: Unrelated event on the same days: must not be merged with A.

news.headline: Hitachinaka chip plant fire: production halted for second day
news.body: The fire at the Hitachinaka factory is out but the plant remains shut.

news.headline: Insurers warn Red Sea attacks will raise freight costs
news.body: Underwriters say war-risk premiums for ships using the Red Sea will rise again.
news.why: Risk commentary about a known situation: the live run alerted on this kind of article; memory should not. Calling it 'not a disruption' is also fine: either way, no alert.

news.headline: Dockworkers at the Port of Felixstowe begin a week-long strike
news.body: Container handling at Felixstowe has stopped.
news.why: Different event whose suppliers are a subset of A's (6 of 15): overlap alone must not merge them.

news.headline: Heavy flooding hits factories in Taipei
news.body: Floodwater has entered industrial areas around Taipei.

news.headline: Flooding spreads from Taipei to Taichung industrial parks
news.body: Rising water now affects plants in both Taipei and Taichung.
news.why: Same flood, a second supplier now exposed: must alert again.

news.headline: Taichung and Taipei factories still flooded
news.body: Plants in Taipei and Taichung remain shut by floodwater.

news.headline: New wave of attacks on ships in the Red Sea
news.body: Carriers again divert from the Red Sea after fresh attacks.
news.why: Same route, but 44 days after A was last reported: A has closed, so this is a new event.
